persistence_contract.qt_window_preference: home_dashboard_overhaul/settings_dialog_geometry/v4 logical geometry screen identity available bounds and informational DPR with valid v3 migration
persistence_contract.settings_preview: compact five-step calendar palette ramp and live Bible appearance preview only; no embedded dashboard preview

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Settings uses a fixed 72 px header, one native active-page body scroller with no horizontal range, and a fixed 56 px footer beside a 184 px vertical rail; compact top navigation is restricted to the small-screen fallback, with no embedded WebEngine content.

The resizable window defaults to 1080x760 logical px, enforces an 860x640 normal minimum, uses 48 px normal and 24 px constrained-screen margins, migrates only valid at-least-80-percent-visible v3 geometry into logical v4 geometry with screen identity and available bounds, centers a maximum-1264 shell and maximum-1080 page, and retains the parented standard QDialog exec lifecycle.
All four complete decorated windows are captured at 1080x760, 1280x800, and full screen at exactly 100 percent application font. No 720 940 or 150 percent page frames belong to the Settings profile.

Accurate dirty count, Discard changes, Close, Save changes, Saving, two-second Saved, validation, and generic persistence failure feedback use a reserved error region plus a separate fixed 56 px action row outside the page scroller; failure retains staged values and leaves Save enabled.

Events proves bounded empty, populated, editor-open, searched, no-results, archived, and long-title states with a labeled sort control, complete selected-tab search, one context-appropriate Add event CTA, and no persistent row selection.

Bible proves short, long, valid custom, invalid custom, and long-row states with one compact live appearance preview, equal-width color-source segments, one inline validation error, a complete filtered verse model, clamped two-line excerpts, and no unexplained result cap.

About proves Version and support, Privacy and legal, and Backup and recovery cards, manifest-derived Supports Anki Desktop 26.8 wording, local diagnostics feedback, byte-exact Scripture attribution, and complete recovery content.

Dirty, discard, child close confirmation, saving, successful save, production-formatted failure, clean legacy Calendar routing, fresh-open and clamped geometry, timer-free page switching, and controlled restart are proven; legacy geometry, monitor, and compact fallback remain structured assertions, while exact-package macOS full-screen opening from both menu and Dashboard gear must pass without a desktop or Space switch in a required structured manual result rather than extra PNGs.

Application-relative role fonts remain at least 10 px at the 100 percent baseline, standard controls use 32-to-34 px targets, icon controls remain at least 28 px square, and alternate-font captures are explicitly outside this minimal profile.

The centered transparent root remains in normal flow at min(1160px, calc(100% - 32px)), with one add-on-owned 30 px top margin producing a measured 28-to-30 px deck-to-dashboard gap, a 14 px desktop column gap, a 360 px rail, and no root viewport-height or overflow clipping.
A visible bottom-action row is detected whether normally positioned, fixed, or sticky and drives root padding and document scroll padding by measured height plus 24 px; 60 px is fallback height only.

At desktop width the 360 px rail uses 12 px gaps and a 352 px minimum-height 2-by-2 summary grid with equal rows and columns, minimum-170 px cards, 14 px 12 px 13 px card padding, 4 px metric row gaps, explicit minmax(0, 1fr) max-content rows, a 10 px target column gap, at least 8 px visible label-to-value separation, and no wrapping, clipping, ellipsis, overlap, font reduction, or internal scrolling.

The complete rail stacks below the calendar at root widths of 1008 px or less, the summary grid retains two columns through 589 px and becomes one column at 588 px or less, desktop minimum heights are removed when stacked, and no dashboard component introduces horizontal scrolling or shrinks typography.

Calendar and top summary cards share a top edge; in Month view the approximately 546 px calendar bottom aligns with the Bible card bottom within 2 px, while in Year view the approximately 352 px calendar bottom aligns with the summary-grid bottom within 2 px and does not extend to the distinct lower-right Bible card.
Month and Year reuse a two-column header with 16 px side insets, 12 px bottom padding, a 16 px title-to-toolbar gap, and 8 px between complete toolbar groups without hiding or crowding controls.
Month always renders a 42-cell six-week grid and retains independently visible completion, selection, today, due, and event cues.

Year keeps one real 53-week tree using 10 px square cells at the wide reference, approximately 2 px gaps, and fluid square cells when narrower; the centered heatmap uses 85-to-90 percent of usable calendar content width with complete aligned labels, no 500 px minimum-width floor, no transforms or zoom, and no clipping or internal horizontal scrolling.

The legend has a 36 px minimum height, 10 px 14 px padding, 18 px group gaps, and 6 px inner gaps; details use 12 px 14 px 15 px padding, a 16 px selected-row gap, an 8 px identity gap, and 14 px and 8 px event spacing while browsing, editing, adding, tooltips, date selection, and Most Missed remain intact.

The Bible card keeps 15 px 16 px 14 px padding and auto 1fr auto rows; its centered verse is capped at 300 px, its citation has an 11 px top gap, and its Month-view minimum height is approximately 182 px without changing the existing typography or visual design.
Every theme-specific saved palette ID has separately authored and visually distinct light and dark completion ladders while IDs and selections stay unchanged.
White, black, purple, and image hosts preserve Anki chrome and remain legible without repainting the host.
Production renders the configured verse font, size, and color exactly across responsive layouts.
Schema remains 8 and name sorting is case-insensitive by name, then date and stable ID; ascending and descending retain date semantics.

Today's Progress orders Initial cards due, Total remaining, New remaining, Learning remaining, and Reviews remaining; Initial cards due is the exact progress denominator Cards studied today + Total remaining; the collection-wide queue remains selected-deck independent and enforces Total remaining = New + Learning + Reviews.

Today's Session uses exactly [next rollover - 86400 seconds, next rollover), counts distinct qualifying introductions, counts only explicitly buried cards that are New or currently due/overdue, calculates seconds per answer, and retains the whole-minute-ceiling ETA policy.

Last 7 Days and All Time match Anki 26.8.1 true-retention eligibility and display one half-up whole percentage; Last 7 Days orders Cards studied, Avg cards/day, Retention, New cards studied, and Time spent, with Avg cards/day equal to Cards studied divided by seven fixed scheduler periods and rounded half-up; All Time aligns Cards studied, Avg cards/day, and Retention in the same first three rows; Again rate remains hidden.

Calendar history and selected-day details use the same rollover-relative records, while due forecasting matches Anki's non-new, non-suspended future-due logic including original filtered-deck due dates and future buried cards but excluding buried work due today.
Initial HTML, live refresh, wide Month and Year 2x2 layouts, intermediate and narrow layouts, and restart all expose identical metric values from one canonical snapshot.

Config and manual verse writes are prepared before mutation, previous config and bytes are retained, and a partial failure attempts rollback before a generic user-facing footer error with separately disclosed technical detail.
The reproducible 1.8.7 archive passes its allowlist, safe-path, byte-parity, manifest/assets, secret/link, and exact-installed-hash gates.
Fresh and restarted Anki 26.8 runs prove process, window, filesystem, and sync isolation before interaction.
The exact package and capture-plan hashes are required for native macOS at 100 percent application font and Retina DPR 2; missing macOS evidence is release-blocking.

Windows, Linux, DPR 1, alternate application-font percentages, VoiceOver, forced colors, and reduced-motion work may remain explicitly unrun and nonblocking; no report implies that these surfaces were tested.
